extracted.intended_audience: academic faculty, postdocs, university labs, and university-based early-career researchers interested in partnering with or applying to DARPA
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for universities and academic researchers on how to work with DARPA: where to find opportunities, recommended engagement channels (Proposers Day, DARPAConnect), and eligibility/expectations for specific programs (Young Faculty Award, Innovation Fellowship).

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority on fundamental research and seeds of surprise
rubrics_metrics.description: Basic research is central to identifying seeds of surprise. Together with academic faculty, postdocs, and university labs, our program managers pursue fundamental scientific breakthroughs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Projects and proposals that pursue fundamental scientific breakthroughs and have the potential to produce unexpected ('surprising') technological advances align with DARPA's mission and priorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support for free scientific exchange and publication
rubrics_metrics.description: We fully support free scientific exchange and publication of fundamental research to the maximum extent possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should expect and may plan to publish fundamental research findings; DARPA encourages free scientific exchange subject to program/contract constraints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use appropriate solicitation channels (BAAs, RFPs, RFIs, contracts, grants)
rubrics_metrics.description: Explore open contracts, grants, and other opportunities, including Broad Agency Announcements (BAAs), Requests for Proposals (RFPs), and Requests for Information (RFIs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify and respond to the correct solicitation type for your work; these are the primary mechanisms by which DARPA solicits and funds research from universities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engage via DARPAConnect for proposal support
rubrics_metrics.description: No matter where you are in your journey with us, DARPAConnect is a valuable resource. Get access to a comprehensive curriculum, proposal support, mentoring, and one-on-one coaching.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Early-career and new proposers should use DARPAConnect to prepare stronger proposals through training, mentoring, and individualized assistance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attend Proposers Day to present ideas and get manager input
rubrics_metrics.description: Our program managers welcome input from prospective university partners on new research ideas, emerging technologies, and technology transition efforts. The best way to connect is to attend a Proposers Day event.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prospective performers should attend Proposers Day events to interact with program managers, present ideas, receive clarifying guidance, and learn about priorities—this is the recommended primary engagement channel.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organize challenge teams for competitive opportunities
rubrics_metrics.description: Some of our strongest challenge contenders–and celebrated winners–hail from universities. Does your school have an appetite for competition?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Forming or organizing a university challenge team is a viable path to compete for DARPA challenges; institutions with coordinated teams have historically performed well.

rubrics_metrics.name: Young Faculty Award (YFA) eligibility and mission
rubrics_metrics.description: To nurture the next generation of program managers and performers, each year we invite junior faculty at U.S. academic and nonprofit research institutions to apply for our Young Faculty Award (YFA). Our mission depends on the dedication of exceptional scientists, engineers, and mathematicians to the quest for technological surprise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: YFA is targeted at junior faculty (U.S. academic and nonprofit research institutions). Applicants should be early-career faculty who demonstrate exceptional dedication and potential for high-impact, surprise-producing research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Innovation Fellowship eligibility and purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: The Innovation Fellowship offers early-career scientists the opportunity to develop and guide research in pursuit of breakthrough technologies for national security. The fellowship is open to scientists, engineers, and mathematicians who completed their doctorate within the last five years. In exceptional cases, we also consider candidates with bachelor or master’s degrees in STEM programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should be early-career researchers (typically within five years of PhD) focused on breakthrough technologies; exceptional non-PhD candidates with relevant bachelor’s or master’s degrees may be considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow CMO guidance for contracting and proposal administrative requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The Contract Management Office (CMO) team provides helpful instructions for proposers, including general terms and conditions, grants and agreements, procurement contracts, and other transactions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposers must follow CMO-provided administrative and contractual guidance (terms/conditions, agreement types) to ensure smooth award and contracting; consult CMO early for compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: DARPA selection and award process (review then contract award)
rubrics_metrics.description: After a review process, DARPA selects the winning proposal, notifies applicants, and awards a contract. CMO works closely with awardees throughout the contract signing process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect a review-based selection; successful applicants will enter contracting with CMO support. Prepare proposal and organizational readiness for post-selection contracting steps.
